text.p: Australian bonds slightly underperformed the dollar bloc on Thursday after starring against its partners on Wednesday.

Traders said the market is looking about fair value after its dramatic sell-off in recent weeks on the basis of monetary policy being on hold and recent data suggesting that the economy has picked from the trough of late last year.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries firmed after there were no further major shocks in Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan's assessment of the U.S. economy in his latest Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
U.S. and Canadian debt are also seen benefiting from a flight to quality from the uncertainty surrounding European Monetary Union, Canadian analysts said.
New Zealand bonds took their lead from the U.S., but the market remains cautious ahead of next week's economic projections by the RBNZ.
However, markets generally are expected to be wary of the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report for February late on Friday.
